route: Green-sand vertically parted flaskless moulding, EN-GJS-400-15 as-cast, no cores; machined on a twin-pallet 4-axis HMC (2 clampings).
route_justification: CHOSEN: ductile iron EN-GJS-400-15 green sand. Reasons: fill ratio 0.063 (spindly, branched arms in three directions) — near-net in sand with a 2-part mould and no cores (only 1 undercut face measured), the lowest-cost route at 200k/yr; ductile iron gives 15 % elongation (safety part) without heat treatment.

ALTERNATIVE 1 — forged steel (e.g. 38MnVS6): 2.80 kg finished (density 7.85 vs 7.10), a branched part with S ≈ 0.06 (EN 10243-1 complexity class S4) needs a large flash (typically ≥ 30 % of billet) and a multi-impression die; the bearing bore would be pierced and arms bent/forged in several directions — material alone ≈ (2.8 kg + ~20 % stock + ~35 % flash) ≈ 4.5 kg bar × £1.15 ≈ £5.2 vs £1.06 of iron charge here; expected +£5–8/part. Not costed in detail.

ALTERNATIVE 2 — aluminium (gravity / squeeze cast A356-T6, ~0.96 kg + section increase ~30 % for stiffness): lighter (unsprung mass) but metal at ~£2.98/kg and T6; expected +£3–6/part vs iron. Not costed in detail.

sources.S1: ISO 8062:1994 "Castings — System of dimensional tolerances and machining allowances" (licensed copy hosted at castingquality.com/wp-content/uploads/2010/05/iso-8062.pdf): Table 1 CT values, Table 2 RMA values (grades A–K by largest finished dimension), Annex A Table A.1 CT grades (long series), Annex B Table B.1 RMA grades; Fig. 5/6: R = F + 2RMA + CT/2 (external), R = F − 2RMA − CT/2 (internal). The same RMA values were carried into ISO 8062-3:2007; the 2007/2023 tables themselves were not read (paywalled).
sources.S2: Sandvik Coromant tools catalogue extract "mtmpa01724" (2018, DGI Supply hosted Sandvik_Coromant_7591766_Catalog.pdf): General turning cutting data p.A24 (GC4325, ISO P); Milling with large engagement p.A70 (ISO K, GC3040/GC1020/GC4330, cutter Ø125); CoroDrill 870 cutting data p.A101–A102 (vc by material, fn by diameter).
sources.S3: Sandvik Coromant CoroDrill 860 -GM leaflet (DGI Supply): recommended start values SFM / feed per rev for Ø6 and Ø8 drills by ISO group.
sources.S4: Sandvik Coromant C-2948 "Small part machining" (2004, Sandvik_5743590_Catalog.pdf) p.170–172: CoroMill Plura solid-carbide end mill cutting data (ve m/min by CMC, fz by Dc).
sources.S5: Sandvik Coromant C-1040:167 "Automotive solutions for ISO K" (2016, Sandvik_6878203_Catalog.pdf): CoroMill 425 finishing EN-GJS-600-3 vc 200 m/min, fz 0.23, 16 inserts, n 510 rpm, ap 0.3–0.5; CoroTap 100-KM M6 in CGI vc 15 m/min.
sources.S6: BS EN 10243-1:1999+corr (Steel die forgings — tolerances, drop and press forgings), copy at itforging.com: method (mass, steel group M1/M2, shape complexity S = m_forging/m_envelope, grade F/E), worked example (200 g C45 forging, 78 mm: +1.1/−0.5 mm), 5.2.4: scale pits allowed to half the nominal machining allowance. Table 1 itself is an image and was NOT read.
sources.S7: Engineers Edge, "Design for Forging" (engineersedge.com/manufacturing/forging-design.htm): "machine allowance should be .06 inch for each machined surface"; standard draft ≥ 1°.
sources.S8: StrikoWestofen shaft-melter figures reported by Foundry Management & Technology / GIFA news: guarantee 600 kWh/t (gas) at 720 °C continuous, pigs + returns; 520–560 kWh/t measured; giessereilexikon: 580–900 kWh/t independent.
sources.S9: ABP Induction (E. Doetsch) / foundry-planet: cast-iron induction melting 515–550 kWh/t melt, 570–700 kWh/t including preparation until pouring; theoretical 385–390 kWh/t at 1,480–1,500 °C.
sources.S10: Rate-book note on forge-induction-heater: SMS Elotherm ~500 kW heats ~1,250 kg/h of steel billets to 1,250 °C (0.40 kWh/kg); vendor ranges 280–450 kWh/t (dw-inductionheater.com).
sources.S11: Open University OpenLearn "Gravity die casting": yield "usually 40–60 %"; cylinder heads one every 5 min; accuracy ±0.1–0.2 mm.
sources.S12: US patent 6,344,265 (coated insert) background: nodular cast iron turned at 150–200 m/min, fn 0.4 mm/rev (secondary source, used for turning/boring ISO K where no Sandvik turning row was available).
